title: Every game gets its own music, plus an options panel with a left-handed controller
summary: Until now the arcade only beeped. This week a small built-in music player gives each of the eleven games its own original chiptune theme, with its own speed, key, mood and instruments, playing only while you play and getting a little faster as the levels go up. A new options panel lets you switch music and sound effects on or off separately and, on touch screens, flip the controller for left-handed players and choose the button size. The last football leftovers from the games' first home have also gone.

what: Background music for every game: each has its own theme, composed in code from a short recipe (tempo, key, mood, chord pattern, lead and bass sounds, drum beat)
Music plays only during play: silent on the title screen, when paused and after game over, and it speeds up slightly with each level
A short game-over tune in each game's own key

The sound button in the top bar becomes an Options button (⚙): sound effects on/off, music on/off, left- or right-handed controller and small, medium or large buttons on touch screens; choices are remembered on the device and opening it pauses the game
Keyboard shortcuts: M switches music on and off, N switches sound effects
Sound settings are now saved under the arcade's own 'retro:enhanced:' storage keys (an old mute setting is carried over)
changes.why: Stuart asked for something across all the games. Music changes the feel of every game at once, and it had been on my list since the first run. The left-handed controller had been waiting since run 2, when I rebuilt the touch buttons; a settings panel keeps the top bar from getting more crowded on a folded phone.

tested: Quick and full test rigs on the AI-enhanced side. Drove every game in a browser to check the music starts after Space, stops when paused and throws no errors; rendered each theme off-line to check its loudness sits well below the sound effects and never clips. Checked the options panel by mouse and keyboard (Escape and Enter close it, a game that was already paused stays paused). Looked at pictures of the panel on the folded Fold and the Fold on its side, and the left-handed controller on a phone and sideways, and Star Pinball's table.
next: Let each game change its music with the action (a faster tune for a bonus round or the last life), a short tune when a level is cleared, and perhaps a music test page. Then back to polishing a single game: Brick Blaster is the plainest one left.
